_why: Vendor landing schemas record what a third-party feed sent. An identity constraint on one of these tables is a CLAIM ABOUT THE VENDOR'S DATA, and it can only be true if the vendor said so. On 2026-09-15 a 166-row sample was used to assert (prod_order_no, prod_line_seq) unique on coldlion.prod_detail; the live population falsified it on 2026-09-17 and nine orders stopped landing. Nobody had asked ColdLion, and the answer file was never opened. This guard makes the citation mandatory and machine-checked.
_activation_why: Migrations stamped before this cannot be edited to add a citation: rewriting an applied migration is forbidden here, and several landed before the guard existed. 20260928211543 is the last one grandfathered - it states its authority in prose but not in the machine-readable header. The guard binds work authored from 2026-09-30 onward.
_activation_window: The floor leaves 2026-09-29 unguarded: anything stamped 20260929* skips the check. That is accepted with eyes open rather than overlooked - the tree holds no 20260929 identity migration, and lowering the floor to cover the day would retroactively refuse 20260928211543, which cannot be edited. If a 20260929 identity migration is ever authored, cite its authority in the header anyway; the guard will not ask, and a later reader will need it.
_citation_forms: A citation must resolve to something a reader can open: a register entry id (2.36) or a dated owner ruling ('owner ruling 2026-09-29'). Free prose is refused. TWO LIMITS, both deliberate and both checked by a human reviewer instead. (1) The owner-ruling form is a SHAPE check only - nothing here can resolve a ruling to a document, so a plausible-looking false one passes. The entry-id form IS verified against the register. Prefer it. (2) The guard checks that a cited entry is SETTLED, not that it is ABOUT the table being changed - citing a settled entry from an unrelated endpoint will pass.
_register_parsing: The register is prose, so the parser is deliberately conservative and will sometimes refuse a citation a human would accept. An entry id must sit alone in the FIRST cell of a pipe-table row. Every row carrying the id must read settled, so two rows that disagree read as OPEN. THE STATUS CELL IS THE LAST CELL of the row, and within it the VERDICT is the opening statement - a bolded opening run if there is one, otherwise the whole cell. The settled test and the open test read THE SAME span in the same case-insensitive way, so neither side can see a marker the other cannot. KNOWN LIMIT, NOT CLOSED: because the verdict span stops at the end of a leading bolded run, a caveat written AFTER that run is outside it, so '**Closed.** Pending the vendor on scope B.' reads settled while the same sentence unbolded reads open. BOLDING STILL CHANGES THE ANSWER. An earlier version of this paragraph claimed the opposite, which was wrong. Closing this properly means not parsing prose at all: requiring the register to carry an explicit machine-readable status token before an entry is citable. That is a change to the register as well as to the guard, and it is the recommended next step rather than another marker added to a list. The open-marker list is likewise an enumeration and always will be; a shouted open marker anywhere in the cell vetoes as well, because a status that shouts both ANSWERED and OPEN is reporting a disagreement rather than a verdict. WITHDRAWN, SUPERSEDED and DROPPED are NOT settled: a withdrawn question is one the vendor never answered, and citing it as where the vendor said it is the failure this guard exists to prevent. FOUR WRONG ANSWERS LED TO THIS RULE, each a real defect found in review rather than a hypothetical: reading any cell let a question column settle an entry whose status column did not; reading the whole status cell read entry 2.36 as open because its verdict is followed by a note that a sub-question is still open; reading only SHOUTED markers flipped 2.36 from settled to open when the register reworded its verdict from 'ANSWERED' to 'Fully answered'; and reading the settled side case-insensitively while reading the open side case-sensitively let 'Closed, awaiting reply.' read settled. TWO STANDING CONSEQUENCES, both accepted with eyes open. (1) This guard's answer depends on how the register is WORDED, so rewording a status cell can change whether an existing citation passes. A register edit that rewrites a verdict should be made with that in mind. (2) The test suite asserts fixed verdicts for real entries (2.36, 2.19, 2.25) and pins both recorded wordings of 2.36, so a pull request that reseats one of those verdicts will turn the 'Vendor identity source authority' check red EVEN IF it changes no code. That is intended - a register edit that silently flips a governance answer should be noticed - but it means such a documentation change must update these tests in the same pull request.
